insight: The doctor discusses how their recent study shows that 78% of patients with chronic pain also experience significant stress, thereby affecting their mental well-being.
The patient shares that ever since they injured their leg, they have been unable to sleep more than 4 hours a night, which has led to increased anxiety.
The doctor mentions a study done in 2019 which found that 45 minutes of moderate exercise, 3 times a week, can improve mood and reduce symptoms of depression by up to 30%.
The doctor recommends a local 'Mind-Body Wellness' program available at the downtown community center, which integrates physical therapy with mindfulness techniques to improve overall well-being.
The patient recounts how, since becoming more physically active again, they've noticed a significant decrease in feelings of depression and are feeling more positive overall.
The doctor explains that patients who are physically incapacitated often experience a 50% increase in feelings of loneliness and isolation, which can severely affect their mental health.
